q: Which statement best describes a mole?
key: A counting unit: 6.0221 × 1023 particles of anything
wrong: The mass of 1 g of any substance
The number of atoms in 1 g of any element
The mass of one carbon-12 atom
explanation: A mole is a counting unit: 1 mol = 6.0221 × 1023 particles (Avogadro's number, NA). Its mass depends on what is being counted.

q: You have 1.00 mol of copper atoms and 1.00 mol of sucrose molecules. Which statement is true?
key: They contain the same number of particles, but the sucrose has more mass.
wrong: They have the same mass, because both are 1.00 mol.
The copper contains more particles, because copper atoms are smaller.
The sucrose contains more particles, because each molecule is bigger.
explanation: Both samples contain the same number of particles (6.0221 × 1023). 1.00 mol of sucrose has a mass of 342.297 g; 1.00 mol of copper, 63.55 g.

q: Sodium chloride, NaCl, is an ionic compound. When you count out 1 mol of NaCl, what particles are you counting?
explanation: 1 mol NaCl = 6.0221 × 1023 formula units, each made of one Na+ ion and one Cl− ion.

q: Which phrase names the counted particles correctly?
explanation: Metal elements: atoms. Molecular compounds: molecules. Ionic compounds: formula units. Ions: ions. Only 1 mol of CO2 molecules names the particle correctly.

q: How many aluminum atoms are in 2.50 mol of aluminum?
explanation: 2.50 mol Al × (6.0221 × 1023 Al atoms / 1 mol Al) = 1.51 × 1024 Al atoms (3 significant figures, like 2.50).

q: A silver ring contains 4.65 × 1022 silver atoms. How many moles of silver is that?
explanation: 4.65 × 1022 atoms ÷ 6.0221 × 1023 atoms/mol = 0.0772 mol Ag, a bit less than a tenth of a mole.

q: A single breath at rest (about half a liter of air) holds about 0.0196 mol of gas molecules. How many molecules is that?
explanation: 0.0196 mol × 6.0221 × 1023 molecules/mol = 1.18 × 1022 molecules. Respiratory therapists work with volumes, but every breath is a count of molecules.

q: Which sample contains the greatest number of atoms?
explanation: Same number of molecules (1.0 mol each), so count atoms per particle: CH4 5, H2O 3, O2 2, He 1. 1.0 mol of CH4 has the most atoms, 5.0 mol.

q: A student calculates that 0.50 mol of water contains 8.3 × 10−25 molecules. What went wrong?
key: The student divided by Avogadro's number instead of multiplying.
wrong: The student used the molar mass of water instead of Avogadro's number.
The student should have counted atoms, which would be 3 times larger.
Nothing; half a mole is a very small amount, so the number should be tiny.
explanation: 8.3 × 10−25 is less than one molecule, which is impossible. It is 0.50 ÷ NA: the student divided instead of multiplying. The correct count is 3.0 × 1023 molecules.

q: A glass holds 1.20 × 1024 water molecules. How many moles of water is that?
explanation: 1.20 × 1024 molecules × (1 mol / 6.0221 × 1023 molecules) = 1.99 mol of water.

q: What is Avogadro's number, as printed on the CHEM 3A yellow sheet?
explanation: NA = 6.0221 × 1023 particles per mole, named for Amedeo Avogadro.

q: Which sample contains the greatest number of particles?
explanation: In moles: CO2 0.80; H2O 3.0 × 1023 ÷ NA = 0.50; Fe 0.25; NaCl 4.2 × 1023 ÷ NA = 0.70. 0.80 mol of CO2 has the most particles.

q: Why is the molar mass of an element, in g/mol, the same number as its atomic mass in amu?
key: Avogadro's number was chosen so that one mole of atoms has a mass in grams equal to the atomic mass in amu.
wrong: One gram is defined as one amu.
Every atom has a mass of exactly 1 amu, so the numbers always match.
It is a coincidence that holds only for carbon.
explanation: NA was chosen so that the mass of 1 mol in grams equals the mass of one particle in amu. So one carbon atom averages 12.011 amu and one mole of carbon has a mass of 12.011 g.

q: What is the molar mass of chlorine gas, Cl2? (Cl 35.45)
explanation: Cl2: 2(35.45) = 70.90 g/mol. The answer keeps 2 decimal places, like 35.45.

q: Ammonia, NH3, is used to make most of the nitrogen fertilizer applied in the Valley. What is its molar mass? (N 14.007, H 1.008)
explanation: NH3: 14.007 + 3(1.008) = 17.031 g/mol. So the molar mass is 17.031 g/mol.

q: Calcium chloride, CaCl2, is used in IV solutions and as a road and dust-control salt. What is its formula mass? (Ca 40.08, Cl 35.45)
explanation: CaCl2: 40.08 + 2(35.45) = 110.98 amu per formula unit (and 110.98 g per mole).

q: Milk of magnesia is a suspension of magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)2. What is its molar mass? (Mg 24.31, O 15.999, H 1.008)
Ammonium sulfate, (NH4)2SO4, is a common nitrogen fertilizer on Valley orchards. What is its molar mass? (N 14.007, H 1.008, S 32.06, O 15.999)
Bone mineral is largely calcium phosphate. What is the molar mass of Ca3(PO4)2? (Ca 40.08, P 30.97, O 15.999)
Glucose, C6H12O6, has a molar mass of 180.156 g/mol. Which statement is correct?
key: One glucose molecule has a mass of 180.156 amu, and one mole of glucose has a mass of 180.156 g.
wrong: One glucose molecule has a mass of 180.156 g.
One mole of glucose has a mass of 180.156 amu.
One glucose molecule has a mass of 180.156 g/mol.
explanation: One molecule: 180.156 amu. One mole: 180.156 g. Molar mass, 180.156 g/mol, links the two.

q: Gypsum, calcium sulfate dihydrate (CaSO4·2H2O), is the raw material for the plaster and dental stone used to pour dental models. What is its molar mass? (Ca 40.08, S 32.06, O 15.999, H 1.008)
Reusable hand-warmer packs contain sodium acetate trihydrate, NaC2H3O2·3H2O. What is its molar mass? (Na 22.99, C 12.011, H 1.008, O 15.999)
Aspirin is C9H8O4. What is its molar mass? (C 12.011, H 1.008, O 15.999)
Potassium chloride, KCl, is used in salt substitutes and potassium supplements. What is its molar mass? (K 39.10, Cl 35.45)
Ibuprofen is C13H18O2. What is its molar mass? (C 12.011, H 1.008, O 15.999)
Iron(III) sulfate is Fe2(SO4)3. What is its molar mass? (Fe 55.85, S 32.06, O 15.999)
A student finds the molar mass of sodium carbonate, Na2CO3, as 2(22.99) + 12.011 + 3(15.999) = 105.988. How should the molar mass be reported?
explanation: Addition rule: fewest decimal places among 22.99 (2), 12.011 (3), 15.999 (3), so 2 places: 105.99 g/mol.

q: The table sets up the molar mass of calcium dihydrogen phosphate, Ca(H2PO4)2, a phosphorus fertilizer. What is the molar mass?
explanation: O: 2 × 4 = 8 atoms, 8(15.999) = 127.992. Sum = 234.044, rounded to 2 decimal places = 234.04 g/mol.

q: A saline-solution recipe calls for 12.5 g of sodium chloride (58.44 g/mol). How many moles is that?
explanation: 12.5 g NaCl × (1 mol NaCl / 58.44 g NaCl) = 0.214 mol (3 significant figures, like 12.5).

q: Calcium carbonate, CaCO3 (100.09 g/mol), is the active ingredient in many antacids. What is the mass of 0.475 mol of it?
explanation: 0.475 mol × (100.09 g / 1 mol) = 47.5 g of CaCO3.

q: A fasting blood glucose is reported as 126 mg/dL. Glucose, C6H12O6, has a molar mass of 180.156 g/mol. What is this value in mmol/L?
explanation: 126 mg/dL × 10 dL/L = 1260 mg/L; 1260 mg/L ÷ 180.156 mg/mmol = 6.99 mmol/L. (Context only; use the units on the facility's meter.)

q: A regular-strength aspirin tablet contains 325 mg of aspirin, C9H8O4 (180.159 g/mol). How many millimoles of aspirin is that?
explanation: 325 mg × (1 mmol / 180.159 mg) = 1.80 mmol of aspirin. (Context only; this is not dosing guidance.)

q: How many ammonia molecules are in 3.50 g of NH3 (17.031 g/mol)?
explanation: 3.50 g × (1 mol / 17.031 g) × (6.0221 × 1023 molecules / 1 mol) = 1.24 × 1023 molecules.

q: A cup of coffee holds about 2.85 × 1020 molecules of caffeine, C8H10N4O2 (194.194 g/mol). What mass of caffeine is that, in grams?
explanation: 2.85 × 1020 ÷ 6.0221 × 1023 = 4.733 × 10−4 mol; × 194.194 g/mol = 0.0919 g of caffeine (about 92 mg).

q: On the mole road map, how do you get from grams of a substance to the number of molecules?
key: Two steps: divide by molar mass to get moles, then multiply by Avogadro's number.
wrong: One step: multiply grams by Avogadro's number.
One step: divide grams by the molar mass.
Two steps: multiply by molar mass, then divide by Avogadro's number.
explanation: grams → (÷ molar mass) → moles → (× 6.0221 × 1023) → molecules: two steps, through moles.

q: Nitrous oxide, N2O (44.013 g/mol), is the “laughing gas” used for sedation in some dental offices. What is the mass of one N2O molecule?
explanation: 44.013 g/mol ÷ 6.0221 × 1023 molecules/mol = 7.3086 × 10−23 g per molecule (5 significant figures, since 44.013 and 6.0221 both have 5).

q: An oral potassium supplement provides 8.00 mmol of potassium chloride, KCl (74.55 g/mol). What mass of KCl is that, in milligrams?
explanation: 8.00 mmol × (74.55 mg / 1 mmol) = 596 mg of KCl. (Context only; follow the order and the label.)

q: What is the mass of 2.75 × 1023 iron atoms? (Fe 55.85)
explanation: 2.75 × 1023 atoms ÷ 6.0221 × 1023 atoms/mol = 0.4567 mol; × 55.85 g/mol = 25.5 g Fe.

q: You have 10.0 g of each of these gases. Which sample contains the most molecules?
explanation: moles = grams ÷ molar mass, so equal masses give the most moles for the smallest molar mass: CH4 (0.623 mol, versus 0.587 NH3, 0.555 H2O, 0.227 CO2).

q: Thyroxine, C15H11I4NO4 (776.86 g/mol), is the main hormone made by the thyroid gland. A daily thyroid-replacement dose is on the order of 0.150 mg. How many thyroxine molecules are in 0.150 mg?
explanation: 1.50 × 10−4 g × (1 mol / 776.86 g) × (6.0221 × 1023 / 1 mol) = 1.16 × 1017 molecules. Even a tiny tablet dose is an enormous number of molecules.

q: Which conversion factor changes grams of NaCl into moles of NaCl?
explanation: g NaCl × (1 mol NaCl / 58.44 g NaCl) = mol NaCl.

q: A vial contains 1.00 g of calcium gluconate, C12H22CaO14 (430.37 g/mol). How many millimoles of calcium gluconate is that?
explanation: 1.00 g × (1 mol / 430.37 g) = 2.324 × 10−3 mol = 2.32 mmol. (Context only; not dosing guidance.)

q: Complete the road-map table for ethanol, C2H5OH. How many molecules are in 11.5 g?
explanation: Moles: 11.5 ÷ 46.069 = 0.2496 mol. Molecules: 0.2496 × 6.0221 × 1023 = 1.50 × 1023 molecules.

q: Which sample has the greatest mass? Use the molar masses H2O 18.015, CO2 44.009, NH3 17.031, and C6H12O6 180.156 g/mol.
explanation: Masses: C6H12O6 18 g, H2O 9.0 g, CO2 8.8 g, NH3 8.5 g. 0.10 mol of glucose has the greatest mass: the most moles is not always the most grams.

q: How many moles of oxygen atoms are in 1 mol of sulfuric acid, H2SO4?
explanation: 1 mol H2SO4 × (4 mol O / 1 mol H2SO4) = 4 mol O.

q: Which conversion factor gives moles of hydrogen atoms from moles of glucose, C6H12O6?
explanation: 12 mol H / 1 mol C6H12O6. This exact ratio never limits significant figures.

q: How many moles of oxygen atoms are in 0.350 mol of calcium nitrate, Ca(NO3)2?
explanation: 0.350 mol Ca(NO3)2 × (6 mol O / 1 mol Ca(NO3)2) = 2.10 mol O.

q: How many hydrogen atoms are in 0.125 mol of ammonia, NH3?
Calcium chloride, CaCl2, dissolves into Ca2+ and Cl− ions. How many ions in total are released by 0.0450 mol of CaCl2?
explanation: 1 Ca2+ + 2 Cl− = 3 ions per formula unit. 0.0450 mol × 3 = 0.135 mol ions = 8.13 × 1022 ions.

q: Rust is mostly iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3. What mass of iron is in 0.400 mol of Fe2O3? (Fe 55.85, O 15.999)
explanation: 0.400 mol × (2 mol Fe / 1 mol Fe2O3) × (55.85 g Fe / 1 mol Fe) = 44.7 g Fe.

q: An iron supplement tablet contains 325 mg of ferrous fumarate, FeC4H2O4 (169.91 g/mol). How many milligrams of elemental iron does it provide? (Fe 55.85)
explanation: 325 mg × (1 mmol / 169.91 mg) × (1 mmol Fe / 1 mmol) × (55.85 mg / 1 mmol Fe) = 107 mg Fe, about a third of the tablet's mass. (Context only; follow the label.)

q: A calcium supplement tablet contains 1.25 g of calcium carbonate, CaCO3 (100.09 g/mol). What mass of calcium does it provide? (Ca 40.08)
explanation: 1.25 g × (1 mol / 100.09 g) × (1 mol Ca / 1 mol) × (40.08 g / 1 mol Ca) = 0.501 g Ca (about 500 mg). (Context only; follow the label.)

q: A children's fluoride supplement tablet contains 2.21 mg of sodium fluoride, NaF (41.99 g/mol). How many milligrams of fluoride does it provide? (F 18.998)
explanation: 2.21 mg × (1 mmol / 41.99 mg) × (1 mmol F / 1 mmol NaF) × (18.998 mg / 1 mmol F) = 1.00 mg F. (Context only; supplements are prescribed by a dentist or physician.)

q: A CT contrast dose contains 32.4 g of iohexol, C19H26I3N3O9 (821.13 g/mol). What mass of iodine does it contain? (I 126.90)
explanation: 32.4 g × (1 mol / 821.13 g) × (3 mol I / 1 mol) × (126.90 g / 1 mol I) = 15.0 g I, almost half the mass of the drug.

q: Urea, CO(NH2)2 (60.056 g/mol), is a high-nitrogen fertilizer. What mass of nitrogen is in 125 g of urea? (N 14.007)
explanation: 125 g × (1 mol / 60.056 g) × (2 mol N / 1 mol) × (14.007 g / 1 mol N) = 58.3 g N, about 46.6% of the urea, matching its 46-0-0 grade.

q: To find the grams of oxygen in 2.00 mol of CO2, which molar mass should you use for oxygen in the last step?
key: 15.999 g/mol, because the formula counts O atoms
wrong: 44.009 g/mol, the molar mass of CO2
explanation: 2.00 mol CO2 × 2 = 4.00 mol O atoms; × 15.999 g/mol = 64.0 g O.

q: Ammonium phosphate, (NH4)3PO4, is a fertilizer. How many moles of hydrogen atoms are in 0.150 mol of it?
explanation: 0.150 mol × (12 mol H / 1 mol (NH4)3PO4) = 1.80 mol H.

q: A sample of aluminum sulfate, Al2(SO4)3, contains 0.900 mol of oxygen atoms. How many moles of Al2(SO4)3 is that?
explanation: 0.900 mol O × (1 mol Al2(SO4)3 / 12 mol O) = 0.0750 mol Al2(SO4)3.

q: How many sodium ions are in 1.00 g of sodium chloride, NaCl (58.44 g/mol)?
explanation: 1.00 g × (1 mol / 58.44 g) × (1 mol Na+ / 1 mol NaCl) × 6.0221 × 1023 = 1.03 × 1022 Na+ ions.

q: The table uses the subscripts of calcium phosphate, Ca3(PO4)2, to find moles of each element in 0.200 mol of the compound. What belongs in the cell marked ?
explanation: O atoms per formula unit = 2 × 4 = 8, so 0.200 mol × 8 = 1.60 mol O.

q: When sodium reacts with chlorine to form sodium chloride, what happens to sodium's single valence electron?
key: It transfers to chlorine, forming Na+ and Cl− ions.
wrong: It is shared equally between Na and Cl in a covalent bond.
Chlorine gives an electron to sodium, forming Na− and Cl+ ions.
It leaves sodium, but chlorine stays neutral, so only Na+ forms.
explanation: Na · + Cl (7 dots) → Na+ + Cl− (8 dots). The electron transfers from Na to Cl, and the attraction between the ions is the ionic bond.

q: Which pair of elements is most likely to form an ionic bond?
explanation: Metal + nonmetal means electron transfer: Mg and O form the ionic compound MgO. (Their electronegativity difference, 3.5 − 1.2 = 2.3, is also above 2.0.)

q: When calcium and oxygen form calcium oxide, CaO, how many electrons does each calcium atom lose, and how many does each oxygen atom gain?
explanation: Ca (group 2) → Ca2+ by losing 2; O (6 valence electrons) → O2− by gaining 2. Ca loses 2, O gains 2: electrons lost = electrons gained, CaO.

q: Aluminum and fluorine form an ionic compound. How many fluorine atoms are needed to accept the electrons from one aluminum atom?
explanation: Al → Al3+ + 3 e−; each F + 1 e− → F−. Electrons lost (3) = electrons gained (3 × 1), so 3 F atoms: AlF3.

q: In the magnesium-oxide lab (Section 6.7), some magnesium reacts with nitrogen in the air to form magnesium nitride. Each Mg atom loses 2 electrons and each N atom gains 3. Which formula makes electrons lost equal electrons gained?
explanation: 6 electrons: 3 Mg × 2 lost = 2 N × 3 gained. Formula Mg3N2, the same one swap-drop gives from Mg2+ and N3−.

q: Which compound is a base (a metal hydroxide)?
explanation: Salts, bases, and metal oxides are the three ionic types. KOH (K+ and OH−) is the base; KCl is a salt, K2O a metal oxide, and CH3OH a molecular compound.

q: Quicklime, CaO, reacts with water to form slaked lime: CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2. How are CaO and Ca(OH)2 classified?
key: CaO is a metal oxide; Ca(OH)2 is a base.
wrong: CaO is a base; Ca(OH)2 is a metal oxide.
CaO is a salt; Ca(OH)2 is a metal oxide.
explanation: CaO (Ca2+, O2−) is a metal oxide; Ca(OH)2 (Ca2+, 2 OH−) is a base.

q: Which property is typical of an ionic compound such as sodium chloride?
key: A hard, brittle solid with a high melting point
wrong: A soft solid that melts below 100 °C
A solid that conducts electricity well
A substance made of separate NaCl molecules
explanation: Ionic solids are lattices of cations and anions: hard, brittle, high-melting, and conducting only when melted or dissolved.

q: Which sample conducts electricity?
key: Calcium chloride melted at high temperature
explanation: Only an ionic compound that is melted or dissolved has moving ions. Melted calcium chloride conducts; the solid does not, and sugar (molecular) never forms ions.

q: How many valence electrons are in phosphorus trichloride, PCl3?
explanation: P: 5; Cl: 3 × 7 = 21. Total = 26 valence electrons.

q: How many valence electrons are in the hydronium ion, H3O+?
explanation: 6 + 3(1) − 1 = 8 valence electrons for H3O+.

q: How many valence electrons are in the phosphate ion, PO43−?
explanation: 5 + 4(6) + 3 = 32 valence electrons for PO43−.

q: Which atom is the central atom in oxygen difluoride, OF2?
key: O, because it appears once and is less electronegative than F
wrong: F, because it is the most electronegative element
Either atom; the skeleton does not matter for a three-atom molecule
explanation: O is central: F–O–F, with two lone pairs on O and three on each F (20 electrons).

q: The Lewis structure of PCl3 has P in the center with three P–Cl bonds. How many lone pairs does the whole molecule have?
explanation: 26 − 3(2) = 20 nonbonding electrons = 10 lone pairs (P: 1; each Cl: 3). Check: 3 × 2 + 10 × 2 = 26.

q: Hydrofluoric acid gel is used to etch porcelain veneers in dental offices. Which describes the Lewis structure of hydrogen fluoride, HF?
key: H–F, with three lone pairs on F
wrong: H–F, with three lone pairs on F and one lone pair on H
H=F, with two lone pairs on F
H–F, with four lone pairs on F
explanation: 1 + 7 = 8 electrons: H–F with three lone pairs on F. (Context only; HF is extremely hazardous to skin.)

q: Which describes the Lewis structure of nitrogen gas, N2, which makes up 78% of air?
key: N≡N, with one lone pair on each N
wrong: N=N, with two lone pairs on each N
N–N, with three lone pairs on each N
explanation: 2 × 5 = 10 electrons. A single bond leaves N short, so lone pairs move into bonds until N≡N with one lone pair on each N (6 + 2 + 2 = 10).

q: Acetylene (ethyne), the fuel in welding torches, is H–C≡C–H. How many bonds does each carbon atom form, counting a triple bond as three?
explanation: Each C: 1 (C–H) + 3 (C≡C) = 4 bonds, 8 electrons, no lone pairs. Total 5 bonding pairs = 10 electrons = 2(4) + 2(1).

q: Methanol, CH3OH, has 14 valence electrons. Which structure is correct?
key: H3C–O–H, with two lone pairs on O
wrong: H3C–H–O, with three lone pairs on O
H3C–O–H, with three lone pairs on O
explanation: 4 + 4(1) + 6 = 14 electrons: H3C–O–H with two lone pairs on O. Check: 5 × 2 + 2 × 2 = 14.

q: Phosgene, COCl2, has C as the central atom and 24 valence electrons. Which Lewis structure is correct?
key: C single-bonded to each Cl and double-bonded to O; 2 lone pairs on O and 3 on each Cl
wrong: C single-bonded to O and to each Cl; 3 lone pairs on O and 3 on each Cl
C double-bonded to O and to one Cl, single-bonded to the other Cl; 2 lone pairs on O, 2 on the double-bonded Cl, 3 on the other Cl
C single-bonded to O and to each Cl; 1 lone pair on C, 3 on O, and 3 on each Cl
explanation: Single bonds use 6, lone pairs on O and Cl use 18 (24 total), but C has only 6. One O lone pair moves into a bond: C=O with two C–Cl bonds. O forms 2 bonds (HONC), Cl forms 1.

q: Which describes the Lewis structure of the ammonium ion, NH4+?
key: N bonded to four H atoms, no lone pairs, in brackets with a 1+ charge
wrong: N bonded to four H atoms, one lone pair on N, in brackets with a 1+ charge
N bonded to three H atoms, one lone pair on N, and the fourth H bonded to another H
N bonded to four H atoms, no lone pairs, in brackets with a 1− charge
explanation: NH4+: 5 + 4(1) − 1 = 8 electrons = four N–H bonds and no lone pairs, drawn as [NH4]+.

q: Ethylene, C2H4, is the gas that ripens fruit in packing-house ripening rooms. It has 12 valence electrons. After you draw a C–C single bond and four C–H bonds, how many electrons are left, and what do you do with them?
key: 2 are left; they become a second C–C bond, making C=C
wrong: 2 are left; add 2 more electrons so each C can have a lone pair
None are left; the structure with single bonds is finished
7 are left; place them as lone pairs on the carbons
explanation: 12 − 5(2) = 2 left. With single bonds each C has 6 electrons, so the last pair becomes a second C–C bond: H2C=CH2, 6 bonding pairs = 12 electrons.

q: How many electrons are shared in the triple bond of N2?
explanation: N≡N: 3 lines × 2 = 6 electrons shared. The more pairs shared, the shorter and stronger the bond.

q: In formaldehyde, CH2O, carbon has two C–H bonds and one C=O double bond. How many electron groups surround the carbon?
explanation: C: two C–H bonds + one C=O = 3 groups, no lone pairs: trigonal planar, 120°.

q: A central atom has 3 electron groups, and 1 of them is a lone pair. What is the molecular shape?
explanation: 3 groups, 1 lone pair: bent, about 120° (electron geometry trigonal planar).

q: Phosphine, PH3, is a fumigant gas used on stored grain and nuts. P has three P–H bonds and one lone pair. What is its shape?
explanation: 4 groups, 1 lone pair: trigonal pyramidal, about 109.5°. (Context only; phosphine is highly toxic.)

q: Water, H2O, has two O–H bonds and two lone pairs on O. What are its electron-group geometry and its molecular shape?
wrong: trigonal planar electron geometry; bent shape
explanation: O: 2 bonds + 2 lone pairs = 4 groups: tetrahedral electron geometry, bent shape (about 109.5°; measured 104.5°).

q: Ground-level ozone, O3, is the main summer smog pollutant in the San Joaquin Valley. Its central O atom has one double bond, one single bond, and one lone pair. What is the shape of O3?
explanation: Central O: 1 double + 1 single + 1 lone pair = 3 groups, 1 lone pair: bent, about 120°.

q: Methane, CH4, the main component of natural gas and of biogas from dairy digesters, has four C–H bonds and no lone pairs. What is the H–C–H bond angle?
explanation: 4 groups, 0 lone pairs: tetrahedral, 109.5°.

q: In acetylene, H–C≡C–H, what is the shape around each carbon atom?
explanation: Each C: 1 single + 1 triple = 2 groups, no lone pairs: linear, 180°. The whole molecule is a straight line.

q: In carbon tetrachloride, CCl4, each Cl has three lone pairs. How many electron groups are on the central carbon?
explanation: C: 4 bonds, 0 lone pairs = 4 groups; tetrahedral, 109.5°. Lone pairs on outer atoms do not change the shape.

q: Complete the row for sulfur dichloride, SCl2, whose S atom has two S–Cl bonds and two lone pairs.
explanation: SCl2: 4 groups / 2 lone pairs: bent, about 109.5°, the same pattern as H2O.

q: Which molecule is trigonal planar?
explanation: Only CH2O has 3 groups and 0 lone pairs. NH3 and PCl3 are trigonal pyramidal (4 groups, 1 lone pair); O3 is bent.

q: Why do CH4 and NH3 have different shapes, even though both central atoms have four electron groups?
key: The shape names only atom positions; N has a lone pair in place of a fourth atom.
wrong: N has fewer electron groups than C.
Lone pairs do not take up any space around the central atom.
C is larger than N, so its bonds spread out more.
explanation: Both have 4 groups (tetrahedral electron geometry), but the shape names only atoms: CH4 tetrahedral; NH3 (1 lone pair) trigonal pyramidal.

q: The hydronium ion, H3O+, has three O–H bonds and one lone pair on O. What is its shape?
explanation: H3O+: 4 groups, 1 lone pair: trigonal pyramidal, about 109.5°.

q: Which of these elements is the most electronegative? (Yellow-sheet values are in the feedback.)
explanation: O 3.5 > N 3.0 = Cl 3.0 > S 2.5. O is the most electronegative of these.

q: Which statement describes the periodic trend in electronegativity?
key: It increases across a period and decreases down a group.
wrong: It decreases across a period and increases down a group.
It increases across a period and increases down a group.
It is about the same for every element in a group.
explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group; fluorine (4.0) is highest.

q: Nitrogen dioxide from vehicle exhaust helps form the Valley's summer ozone. What is ΔEN for an N–O bond, and what kind of bond is it? (N 3.0, O 3.5)
explanation: ΔEN = 3.5 − 3.0 = 0.5, polar covalent; O carries δ−.

q: Classify the C–H bond using the yellow-sheet values (C 2.5, H 2.1).
explanation: ΔEN = 2.5 − 2.1 = 0.4: nonpolar covalent. Remember from lecture: C–H is essentially nonpolar.

q: In fluorapatite, the fluoride-strengthened mineral of tooth enamel, fluoride ions sit next to calcium ions. Classify the Ca–F bond. (Ca 1.0, F 4.0)
explanation: ΔEN = 4.0 − 1.0 = 3.0, ionic: fluorapatite is an ionic crystal of Ca2+, PO43−, and F−.

q: In an O–H bond, which atom carries the partial negative charge (δ−), and which way does the dipole arrow point? (O 3.5, H 2.1)
key: O is δ−; the arrow points toward O
wrong: H is δ−; the arrow points toward H
O is δ−; the arrow points toward H
Neither; the O–H bond is nonpolar
explanation: O–H: ΔEN = 1.4, polar covalent. O is δ−, and the dipole arrow points toward O (cross at H).

q: Which bond is the most polar? (H 2.1, C 2.5, N 3.0, O 3.5, Cl 3.0)
explanation: C–Cl 0.5 < N–H 0.9 < C–O 1.0 < O–H 1.4. O–H is the most polar.

q: Carbon dioxide, O=C=O, has polar C=O bonds. Is the CO2 molecule polar or nonpolar?
key: Nonpolar: it is linear, and the two equal bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel.
wrong: Polar, because each C=O bond is polar.
Polar, because oxygen is more electronegative than carbon.
Nonpolar, because ΔEN for C=O is 0.4 or less.
explanation: C has 2 groups and no lone pairs: linear. Equal C=O dipoles (ΔEN 1.0) point opposite ways and cancel: CO2 is nonpolar.

q: Which molecule is polar?
explanation: CH3Cl is asymmetrical (one Cl, three H), so it is polar. CCl4 and CH4 are symmetrical; Cl2 has no polar bond.

q: In the lungs, O2 and CO2 cross the thin, fatty membranes of the alveoli and capillaries very quickly. Which statement explains this?
wrong: Both are polar molecules, like water.
CO2 is polar and O2 is nonpolar.
Both are ionic compounds that dissolve in the membrane.
explanation: Both are small nonpolar molecules, so they slip through the nonpolar membrane; ions such as Na+ need protein channels.

q: Which molecule is nonpolar even though its bonds are polar?
explanation: CF4: polar C–F bonds (ΔEN 1.5), but the symmetrical tetrahedral shape cancels them.

q: Water is bent. Suppose instead it were linear, H–O–H in a straight line. What would be true?
key: It would be nonpolar, because the two equal O–H dipoles would cancel.
wrong: It would still be polar, because the O–H bonds are polar.
It would become an ionic compound.
It would be nonpolar, because the O–H bonds would stop being polar.
explanation: A linear H–O–H would be nonpolar (dipoles cancel). Because real water is bent, the dipoles add and water is polar.

q: Food labels list sodium, not salt. What is the mass percent of sodium in sodium chloride, NaCl (58.44 g/mol)? (Na 22.99)
Ammonium sulfate, (NH4)2SO4 (132.13 g/mol), is a nitrogen fertilizer used on Valley orchards. What is its mass percent of nitrogen? (N 14.007)
Bone mineral is largely calcium phosphate, Ca3(PO4)2 (310.17 g/mol). What is its mass percent of calcium? (Ca 40.08)
Ethanol, C2H5OH (46.069 g/mol), is the alcohol in hand sanitizer. What is its mass percent of carbon? (C 12.011)
Iron tablets often contain ferrous sulfate heptahydrate, FeSO4·7H2O (278.01 g/mol). What percent of this compound's mass is iron? (Fe 55.85)
explanation: %Fe = 55.85 ÷ 278.01 × 100% = 20.09%. A 325 mg tablet of this hydrate holds about 65 mg of iron. (Context only.)

q: One sample of pure sodium chloride comes from sea salt, and another is mined rock salt from a different continent. What does the law of constant composition say about them?
key: Both have the same mass percent of sodium.
wrong: The larger sample has the higher mass percent of sodium.
Their percents differ, because they come from different places.
Both are 50% sodium, because NaCl has one Na and one Cl.
explanation: Law of constant composition (definite proportions): every pure sample of NaCl has the same mass percent of sodium.

q: A student heats 1.308 g of zinc powder with excess sulfur. The zinc sulfide product has a mass of 1.950 g. What is the mass percent of zinc in the product?
Heating 1.200 g of copper in air produces 1.502 g of a black copper oxide. What is the mass percent of oxygen in the oxide?
The table shows a student's data from the magnesium-oxide lab (Experiment 5a). What is the mass percent of magnesium in the product?
A compound of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen is 54.53% C and 9.15% H by mass, and the rest is oxygen. What is its mass percent of oxygen?
explanation: %O = 100% − 54.53% − 9.15% = 36.32% (2 decimal places, from the subtraction).

q: Butane, C4H10, is lighter fluid. What is its empirical formula?
explanation: C4H10 ÷ 2 = C2H5.

q: Which two compounds have the same empirical formula?
explanation: C2H2 (acetylene) and C6H6 (benzene) are both CH.

q: In a lab, 1.020 g of aluminum reacts with oxygen to form 1.927 g of aluminum oxide. What is the empirical formula of the oxide? (Al 26.98, O 15.999)
explanation: Al 0.03781 mol : O 0.05669 mol = 1 : 1.499; × 2 = 2 : 3. Al2O3, as Al3+ and O2− predict.

q: An oxide of sulfur is 50.05% S and 49.95% O by mass. What is its empirical formula? (S 32.06, O 15.999)
Magnetite, a magnetic iron ore, is 72.36% Fe and 27.64% O by mass. What is its empirical formula? (Fe 55.85, O 15.999)
Lactic acid, which muscle cells make (as lactate) during hard exercise, has the empirical formula CH2O and a molar mass of 90.08 g/mol. What is its molecular formula? (C 12.011, H 1.008, O 15.999)
The table gives the mass percent composition of caffeine, whose molar mass is 194.19 g/mol. What is its molecular formula? (C 12.011, H 1.008, N 14.007, O 15.999)
explanation: Empirical formula C4H5N2O, 97.097 g/mol; n = 194.19 ÷ 97.097 = 2.000: C8H10N4O2.

q: Epsom salt is magnesium sulfate hydrate, MgSO4·xH2O. Heating 3.000 g of it leaves 1.465 g of anhydrous MgSO4 (120.37 g/mol). What is x? (H2O 18.015 g/mol)
explanation: 1.535 g ÷ 18.015 g/mol = 0.08521 mol H2O; 1.465 g ÷ 120.37 g/mol = 0.01217 mol MgSO4; ratio 7.00: x = 7, MgSO4·7H2O.

q: A phosphorus oxide is 43.64% P and 56.36% O by mass. What is its empirical formula? (P 30.97, O 15.999)
Copper wire (2.538 g) is heated with sulfur until all the copper has reacted, giving 3.178 g of a copper sulfide. What is its empirical formula? (Cu 63.55, S 32.06)
explanation: Cu 0.03994 mol : S 0.01996 mol = 2.001 : 1: Cu2S (copper(I) sulfide).

q: Which observation is the best evidence that a chemical reaction has occurred?
key: Two clear, colorless solutions are mixed, and a cloudy yellow solid forms.
wrong: A pot of water on the stove forms bubbles as it heats.
A spoonful of sugar disappears when it is stirred into hot tea.
An ice cube melts into a puddle on the counter.
explanation: A new solid appearing from clear solutions is a precipitate, one of the four signs of reaction (gas, precipitate, color change, energy change).

q: Each of these fizzes. Which one is a physical change, not a chemical reaction?
key: A bottle of soda is opened, and dissolved carbon dioxide escapes as bubbles.
wrong: An antacid tablet containing calcium carbonate is dropped into hydrochloric acid.
Hydrogen peroxide is poured on a cut, where the enzyme catalase breaks it into water and oxygen gas.
Baking soda is stirred into vinegar.
explanation: Opening a soda only releases gas that was already dissolved; the other three make new substances, including a new gas.

q: Barium chloride solution is mixed with magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) solution: BaCl2(aq) + MgSO4(aq) → BaSO4(s) + MgCl2(aq). What does the label (s) after BaSO4 tell you?
key: BaSO4 forms as a solid, a precipitate.
wrong: BaSO4 stays dissolved in the water.
BaSO4 is formed as a gas.
Only a single unit of BaSO4 forms.
explanation: (s) = solid, (l) = liquid, (g) = gas, (aq) = dissolved in water. BaSO4(s) is a solid precipitate; MgCl2(aq) stays dissolved.

q: How many oxygen atoms are represented by 2 Al2(SO4)3?
explanation: 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 O atoms.

q: In a sealed flask, 2.43 g of magnesium reacts completely with 1.60 g of oxygen gas: 2 Mg(s) + O2(g) → 2 MgO(s). What mass of magnesium oxide forms?
A student heats baking soda, NaHCO3, in an open crucible: 2 NaHCO3(s) → Na2CO3(s) + H2O(g) + CO2(g). Using the data in the table, what total mass of water vapor and carbon dioxide escaped?
explanation: Gases escaped = 31.62 g − 28.52 g = 3.10 g. In a sealed container the total mass would not change.

q: Sulfur dioxide from burning sulfur-containing fuel reacts with oxygen in the air to form sulfur trioxide, a step toward acid rain. Which is the correctly balanced equation?
explanation: O: 2 + 2 = 4 on the left vs 3 on the right; 2 SO3 needs 2 SO2 and one O2. 2 SO2(g) + O2(g) → 2 SO3(g)

q: Balance the equation: Al2(SO4)3(aq) + KOH(aq) → Al(OH)3(s) + K2SO4(aq). What are the coefficients, in order?
Lighter fluid is butane, C4H10. In the balanced equation for its complete combustion, C4H10(g) + O2(g) → CO2(g) + H2O(g), what is the lowest whole-number coefficient of O2?
explanation: 2 C4H10(g) + 13 O2(g) → 8 CO2(g) + 10 H2O(g): O 26 = 16 + 10. The coefficient of O2 is 13.

q: A student balances H2(g) + Cl2(g) → HCl(g) by changing it to H2(g) + Cl2(g) → H2Cl2(g). What is wrong?
key: Changing a subscript makes a different substance; a coefficient of 2 in front of HCl is the fix.
wrong: Nothing is wrong, because the atoms now balance.
The reactants should be written as single atoms, H and Cl, so that HCl balances.
The fix should be a coefficient of 2 in front of H2 instead.
explanation: Never change subscripts. H2(g) + Cl2(g) → 2 HCl(g): H 2 = 2, Cl 2 = 2.

q: Aluminum metal burns in chlorine gas to form solid aluminum chloride. Which balanced equation uses the lowest whole-number coefficients?
explanation: Al + Cl2 → AlCl3: Cl needs a common multiple of 2 and 3, so 3 Cl2 and 2 AlCl3, then 2 Al. 2 Al(s) + 3 Cl2(g) → 2 AlCl3(s)

q: In a blast furnace, solid iron(III) oxide reacts with carbon monoxide gas to form solid iron and carbon dioxide gas. Which equation is correct, balanced, and labeled?
explanation: Fe2O3(s) + 3 CO(g) → 2 Fe(s) + 3 CO2(g). Check: Fe 2 = 2, C 3 = 3, O 6 = 6.

q: Heating mercury(II) oxide releases oxygen gas: 2 HgO(s) → 2 Hg(l) + O2(g). What type of reaction is this?
explanation: One reactant, two products: decomposition, AB → A + B.

q: Nickel wire is placed in silver nitrate solution: Ni(s) + 2 AgNO3(aq) → Ni(NO3)2(aq) + 2 Ag(s). What type of reaction is this?
explanation: Element + compound → new compound + new element: single displacement.

q: What type of reaction is AgNO3(aq) + KBr(aq) → AgBr(s) + KNO3(aq)?
explanation: The cations trade anions: double displacement (a precipitation, since AgBr is insoluble).

q: Which reaction is a combination reaction?
explanation: Only 2 Ca + O2 → 2 CaO makes a single product from two reactants.

q: Calcium metal heated in nitrogen gas forms calcium nitride. Which equation correctly predicts and balances the product?
explanation: Ca2+ + N3− → Ca3N2; 3 Ca(s) + N2(g) → Ca3N2(s).

q: Strontium carbonate is heated strongly, the way limestone is heated to make lime. Which equation shows the decomposition?
explanation: SrCO3(s) → SrO(s) + CO2(g). Sr 1 = 1; C 1 = 1; O 3 = 1 + 2.

q: Aluminum sulfate solution (used to clarify drinking water) is mixed with barium nitrate solution. Which gives the correct formulas of the two products?
explanation: Al(NO3)3 and BaSO4: Al2(SO4)3(aq) + 3 Ba(NO3)2(aq) → 2 Al(NO3)3(aq) + 3 BaSO4(s).

q: A propane space heater run in a closed garage gets too little oxygen and makes carbon monoxide, a poison that binds hemoglobin. Which balanced equation shows this incomplete combustion of propane, C3H8?
explanation: C3H8 → 3 CO + 4 H2O needs 7 O = 3.5 O2; double: 2 C3H8(g) + 7 O2(g) → 6 CO(g) + 8 H2O(g).

q: Rubbing alcohol (isopropyl alcohol, C3H8O) is flammable, which is why it is kept away from oxygen equipment in hospitals. In the balanced equation for its complete combustion, C3H8O(l) + O2(g) → CO2(g) + H2O(g), what is the lowest whole-number coefficient of O2?
explanation: 2 C3H8O(l) + 9 O2(g) → 6 CO2(g) + 8 H2O(g): O 2 + 18 = 20 = 12 + 8. Coefficient of O2: 9.

q: Which reaction is a single-displacement reaction?
explanation: Fe + Pb(NO3)2 → Fe(NO3)2 + Pb fits A + BC → AC + B.

q: Which substance is a nonelectrolyte when dissolved in water?
explanation: Glucose, C6H12O6, dissolves without forming ions: a nonelectrolyte. It travels in blood as whole molecules.

q: A conductivity tester is dipped into four solutions, all at the same concentration. The table shows how brightly its bulb glows. Solution B is most likely which substance?
explanation: Dim glow = weak electrolyte = acetic acid. A could be KCl or HCl; C could be sucrose.

q: Calcium nitrate is a fertilizer used on Valley crops. Which equation shows what happens when it dissolves in water?
explanation: Ca(NO3)2(s) → Ca2+(aq) + 2 NO3−(aq)

q: How many ions in total are released when one formula unit of Al2(SO4)3 dissolves completely?
explanation: Al2(SO4)3(s) → 2 Al3+(aq) + 3 SO42−(aq): 2 + 3 = 5 ions.

q: Use the solubility rules. Which compound is insoluble in water?
explanation: AgI: iodide with Ag+ is an exception, so AgI is insoluble.

q: Kidney stones and the scale in kettles are insoluble salts. Which of these compounds is soluble in water?
explanation: Only K2CO3 has a Group 1 cation; the other three are on the insoluble side of their rows.

q: A barium contrast agent must be insoluble, so that almost no toxic Ba2+ dissolves and is absorbed. By the solubility rules, which barium compound is insoluble?
explanation: BaSO4 is insoluble (sulfate with Ba2+), which is why it is used for X-ray contrast. (Context only.)

q: Which sulfide is insoluble in water?
explanation: ZnS is insoluble; Zn2+ is not on the exception list.

q: Which pair contains two insoluble compounds?
explanation: Pb2+ and Hg22+ are halide exceptions, so PbI2 and Hg2Cl2 are both insoluble.

q: Which statement about strontium fluoride and strontium chloride is correct?
key: SrF2 is insoluble; SrCl2 is soluble.
wrong: SrF2 is soluble; SrCl2 is insoluble.
SrF2 is soluble; SrCl2 is soluble.
SrF2 is insoluble; SrCl2 is insoluble.
explanation: SrF2 is insoluble; SrCl2 is soluble.

q: Copper(II) sulfate solution is mixed with sodium hydroxide solution. Which product is the precipitate?
explanation: CuSO4(aq) + 2 NaOH(aq) → Cu(OH)2(s) + Na2SO4(aq): the blue precipitate is Cu(OH)2.

q: Calcium nitrate solution is mixed with potassium chloride solution. What precipitate forms?
explanation: Both CaCl2 and KNO3 are soluble, so every ion is a spectator: no precipitate (no reaction).

q: Hard-water scale is calcium carbonate. It forms the same way it does when calcium nitrate solution is mixed with potassium carbonate solution. What is the net ionic equation?
explanation: Complete ionic: Ca2+ + 2 NO3− + 2 K+ + CO32− → CaCO3(s) + 2 K+ + 2 NO3−. Net: Ca2+(aq) + CO32−(aq) → CaCO3(s).

q: Zinc chloride solution is mixed with potassium sulfide solution, forming a white precipitate. What is the complete ionic equation?
key: Zn2+(aq) + 2 Cl−(aq) + 2 K+(aq) + S2−(aq) → ZnS(s) + 2 K+(aq) + 2 Cl−(aq)
wrong: Zn2+(aq) + 2 Cl−(aq) + 2 K+(aq) + S2−(aq) → Zn2+(aq) + S2−(aq) + 2 K+(aq) + 2 Cl−(aq)
Zn2+(aq) + Cl−(aq) + K+(aq) + S2−(aq) → ZnS(s) + K+(aq) + Cl−(aq)
Zn2+(aq) + Cl22−(aq) + K22+(aq) + S2−(aq) → ZnS(s) + K22+(aq) + Cl22−(aq)
explanation: Zn2+(aq) + 2 Cl−(aq) + 2 K+(aq) + S2−(aq) → ZnS(s) + 2 K+(aq) + 2 Cl−(aq)

q: Lead(II) acetate solution is mixed with potassium iodide solution, and yellow lead(II) iodide precipitates. What are the spectator ions?
wrong: There are none; all four ions react.
explanation: Net ionic: Pb2+(aq) + 2 I−(aq) → PbI2(s). Spectators: K+ and C2H3O2−.

q: Aluminum hydroxide, an ingredient in some antacids, can be made by mixing aluminum nitrate solution with potassium hydroxide solution. What is the net ionic equation?
explanation: Al3+(aq) + 3 OH−(aq) → Al(OH)3(s); K+ and NO3− are spectators.

q: Which pair of solutions gives no reaction when mixed?
explanation: 2 KNO3 + MgCl2 → 2 KCl(aq) + Mg(NO3)2(aq): all ions are spectators, so KNO3 and MgCl2 give no reaction.

q: Struvite kidney stones contain magnesium and phosphate ions. In the lab, magnesium phosphate precipitates when magnesium chloride solution is mixed with sodium phosphate solution. What is the net ionic equation?
wrong: 3 Mg2+(aq) + 2 PO43−(aq) + 6 Na+(aq) + 6 Cl−(aq) → Mg3(PO4)2(s) + 6 Na+(aq) + 6 Cl−(aq)
explanation: 3 MgCl2(aq) + 2 Na3PO4(aq) → Mg3(PO4)2(s) + 6 NaCl(aq); net: 3 Mg2+(aq) + 2 PO43−(aq) → Mg3(PO4)2(s).

q: The complete ionic equation for mixing silver nitrate and sodium carbonate solutions is 2 Ag+(aq) + 2 NO3−(aq) + 2 Na+(aq) + CO32−(aq) → Ag2CO3(s) + 2 Na+(aq) + 2 NO3−(aq). What is the net ionic equation?
explanation: 2 Ag+(aq) + CO32−(aq) → Ag2CO3(s)

q: Sodium sulfide solution is mixed with copper(II) nitrate solution, and a black solid forms. What is the net ionic equation?
explanation: Na2S(aq) + Cu(NO3)2(aq) → CuS(s) + 2 NaNO3(aq); net: Cu2+(aq) + S2−(aq) → CuS(s).

q: What is the balanced molecular equation for hydrobromic acid reacting with potassium hydroxide?
explanation: HBr(aq) + KOH(aq) → H2O(l) + KBr(aq)

q: Sulfuric acid is neutralized by lithium hydroxide: H2SO4(aq) + 2 LiOH(aq) → 2 H2O(l) + Li2SO4(aq). What is the net ionic equation?
explanation: H+(aq) + OH−(aq) → H2O(l), the same for every strong acid + strong base.

q: Milk of magnesia is a suspension of solid magnesium hydroxide that neutralizes stomach acid (HCl). What is the net ionic equation?
explanation: Complete ionic: Mg(OH)2(s) + 2 H+ + 2 Cl− → Mg2+ + 2 Cl− + 2 H2O. Net: Mg(OH)2(s) + 2 H+(aq) → Mg2+(aq) + 2 H2O(l). (Context only.)

q: Vinegar (acetic acid, a weak acid) reacts with sodium hydroxide solution. What is the net ionic equation?
explanation: Complete ionic: HC2H3O2 + Na+ + OH− → H2O + Na+ + C2H3O2−. Net: HC2H3O2(aq) + OH−(aq) → H2O(l) + C2H3O2−(aq).

q: After swapping partners for potassium carbonate + nitric acid, a student writes carbonic acid, H2CO3(aq), as a product. What should it be replaced with?
wrong: Nothing; H2CO3(aq) is the final product.
explanation: H2CO3 → CO2(g) + H2O(l): K2CO3(aq) + 2 HNO3(aq) → 2 KNO3(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g).

q: Sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3) is a preservative in dried fruit such as golden raisins and apricots. When it reacts with hydrochloric acid, which gas is released?
explanation: NaHSO3(aq) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) + SO2(g): the gas is sulfur dioxide, SO2, the sharp smell of the preservative.

q: Spreading an ammonium fertilizer together with a strong base wastes nitrogen as ammonia gas. Which equation correctly shows ammonium sulfate reacting with potassium hydroxide?
explanation: (NH4)2SO4(aq) + 2 KOH(aq) → K2SO4(aq) + 2 H2O(l) + 2 NH3(g)

q: Solid iron(II) sulfide reacts with hydrochloric acid and gives off a rotten-egg smell. Which is the balanced equation?
explanation: FeS(s) + 2 HCl(aq) → FeCl2(aq) + H2S(g)

q: Which of these solutions gives no reaction when it is mixed with nitric acid, HNO3(aq)?
explanation: KCl: HNO3(aq) + KCl(aq) would give only HCl(aq) and KNO3(aq), so all four ions are spectators and there is no reaction.

q: In Mg(s) + Cl2(g) → MgCl2(s), what happens to magnesium?
key: It loses 2 electrons and is oxidized.
wrong: It gains 2 electrons and is reduced.
It loses 2 electrons and is reduced.
It gains 2 electrons and is oxidized.
explanation: Mg: 0 → +2, so it loses 2 electrons and is oxidized; each Cl: 0 → −1, reduced.

q: Ground-level ozone, O3, is a Valley air pollutant. What is the oxidation number of oxygen in O3?
explanation: O3 is a form of the element oxygen, so each O is 0.

q: Nitrate, NO3−, is a fertilizer ion that can reach well water. What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in NO3−?
explanation: N + 3(−2) = −1 → N = +5.

q: What is the oxidation number of chromium in potassium chromate, K2CrO4?
What is the oxidation number of oxygen in oxygen difluoride, OF2?
explanation: F = −1 (rule 4, before oxygen's rule); O + 2(−1) = 0 → O = +2.

q: In Ni(s) + 2 Ag+(aq) → Ni2+(aq) + 2 Ag(s), which reactant is oxidized?
explanation: Ni: 0 → +2 (oxidized); Ag: +1 → 0 (reduced). Ni is oxidized.

q: The thermite reaction welds railroad rails: 2 Al(s) + Fe2O3(s) → Al2O3(s) + 2 Fe(s). What is the oxidizing agent?
explanation: Al: 0 → +3 (oxidized; reducing agent). Fe: +3 → 0 (reduced). Oxidizing agent: Fe2O3.

q: A welding torch burns acetylene: 2 C2H2(g) + 5 O2(g) → 4 CO2(g) + 2 H2O(g). What is the reducing agent?
explanation: C: −1 → +4 (oxidized); O: 0 → −2 (reduced); H stays +1. Reducing agent: C2H2.

q: How many electrons are transferred in 2 Al(s) + 3 Sn2+(aq) → 2 Al3+(aq) + 3 Sn(s) as written?
explanation: 2 Al → 2 Al3+ + 6 e−; 3 Sn2+ + 6 e− → 3 Sn. 6 electrons.

q: Stainless-steel implants resist corrosion because the chromium in the steel forms a thin protective layer. Where chromium is oxidized, it forms Cr3+. Which is the oxidation half-reaction?
explanation: Cr(s) → Cr3+(aq) + 3 e−

q: Use the half-reactions Al(s) → Al3+(aq) + 3 e− and Ag+(aq) + e− → Ag(s). What is the balanced net equation?
explanation: Al → Al3+ + 3 e−; 3 Ag+ + 3 e− → 3 Ag. Sum: Al(s) + 3 Ag+(aq) → Al3+(aq) + 3 Ag(s).

q: Which reaction is not a redox reaction?
explanation: Only BaCl2 + K2SO4 → BaSO4 + 2 KCl keeps every oxidation number; double displacement is never redox.

q: Copper(II) sulfate solution is sprayed on Valley orchards as a fungicide, and it corrodes iron sprayer tanks. Activity series (most active first): Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Ni, Sn, Pb, H2, Cu, Ag. Does iron react with copper(II) sulfate solution?
wrong: No reaction, because iron is below copper in the series.
explanation: Fe is above Cu: Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s).

q: Activity series (most active first): Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Ni, Sn, Pb, H2, Cu, Ag, Au. Which metal will not react with hydrochloric acid?
explanation: Cu is below H2: no reaction with HCl.

q: Activity series (most active first): Zn, Fe, Ni, Sn, Pb, H2, Cu, Ag, Au. Which metal could recover lead from a solution of lead(II) nitrate?
explanation: Only Zn is above Pb on the list.

q: Activity series (most active first): Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Ni, Sn, Pb. Does lead metal react with zinc chloride solution?
key: No reaction: lead is below zinc.
explanation: Pb is below Zn: no reaction.

q: Activity series (most active first): Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Ni, Sn, Pb, H2, Cu. Which equation correctly shows aluminum reacting with hydrochloric acid?
explanation: 2 Al(s) + 6 HCl(aq) → 2 AlCl3(aq) + 3 H2(g)

q: Activity series (most active first): Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Ni, Sn, Pb, H2, Cu. A metal reacts with nickel(II) nitrate solution but not with zinc nitrate solution. Which metal could it be?
explanation: Between Zn and Ni there is only Fe.

q: Galvanized steel irrigation pipe is coated with zinc, which corrodes in place of the iron. Activity series (most active first): Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Ni. Which net ionic equation shows zinc reacting with Fe2+ ions?
explanation: Zn(s) + Fe2+(aq) → Zn2+(aq) + Fe(s)

q: In the balanced equation 2 H2(g) + O2(g) → 2 H2O(l), what do the coefficients tell you?
key: 2 mol of H2 react with 1 mol of O2 to make 2 mol of H2O.
wrong: 2 g of H2 react with 1 g of O2 to make 2 g of H2O.
2 molecules of H2 and 1 molecule of O2 make 3 molecules of H2O.
Each H2O molecule has 2 H atoms and 1 O atom, so the coefficients repeat the subscripts.
explanation: Coefficients are mole ratios: 2 mol H2 react with 1 mol O2 to make 2 mol H2O.

q: For the combustion of propane, C3H8(g) + 5 O2(g) → 3 CO2(g) + 4 H2O(l), which conversion factor turns moles of O2 into moles of CO2?
explanation: mol O2 × (3 mol CO2 / 5 mol O2) = mol CO2.

q: Nitric acid for fertilizer is made from ammonia. The first step is 4 NH3(g) + 5 O2(g) → 4 NO(g) + 6 H2O(g). How many moles of O2 react with 3.60 mol of NH3?
explanation: 3.60 mol NH3 × (5 mol O2 / 4 mol NH3) = 4.50 mol O2. The mole ratio is exact, so the answer keeps the 3 significant figures of 3.60.

q: In cellular respiration, C6H12O6 + 6 O2 → 6 CO2 + 6 H2O. How many moles of glucose are used when your cells produce 0.480 mol of CO2?
explanation: 0.480 mol CO2 × (1 mol C6H12O6 / 6 mol CO2) = 0.0800 mol C6H12O6.

q: Hydrogen peroxide foams on a cut because an enzyme in blood (catalase) speeds up 2 H2O2(aq) → 2 H2O(l) + O2(g). How many moles of O2 form from 0.856 mol of H2O2?
explanation: 0.856 mol H2O2 × (1 mol O2 / 2 mol H2O2) = 0.428 mol O2.

q: For 2 Mg(s) + O2(g) → 2 MgO(s), a student says, “2 g of Mg react with 1 g of O2.” Which statement corrects the student?
key: 2 mol of Mg (48.62 g) react with 1 mol of O2 (31.998 g); coefficients are mole ratios, not mass ratios.
wrong: The student is right; coefficients give the ratio of grams.
2 g of Mg react with 2 g of O2, because the product has 2 MgO.
1 g of Mg reacts with 2 g of O2, because O2 has two atoms.
explanation: The equation means 2 mol Mg (2 × 24.31 = 48.62 g) react with 1 mol O2 (31.998 g). Coefficients are mole ratios; to compare masses, use molar masses.

q: In N2(g) + 3 H2(g) → 2 NH3(g), 4 mol of reactant molecules make only 2 mol of product. What is conserved in this reaction?
key: The number of each kind of atom, and so the total mass
wrong: The total number of moles of molecules
The number of molecules of each substance
Nothing; 2 mol of product weighs less than 4 mol of reactants
explanation: Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, so atoms and mass are conserved; moles of molecules are not (4 mol → 2 mol).

q: In a blast furnace, iron ore is reduced by carbon monoxide: Fe2O3(s) + 3 CO(g) → 2 Fe(l) + 3 CO2(g). How many moles of CO are needed to produce 1.25 mol of Fe?
explanation: 1.25 mol Fe × (3 mol CO / 2 mol Fe) = 1.88 mol CO.

q: A propane camp stove burns fuel by C3H8(g) + 5 O2(g) → 3 CO2(g) + 4 H2O(l). How many moles of O2 were used if 2.46 mol of H2O formed?
explanation: 2.46 mol H2O × (5 mol O2 / 4 mol H2O) = 3.08 mol O2.

q: The table follows the mole ratio of 4 Al(s) + 3 O2(g) → 2 Al2O3(s), which forms the thin oxide layer that protects aluminum. What belongs in the cell marked ?
explanation: mol O2 = mol Al × 3/4, so 0.80 × 3/4 = 0.60 mol O2.

q: For octane in gasoline, 2 C8H18(l) + 25 O2(g) → 16 CO2(g) + 18 H2O(g). A student converts 0.3150 mol O2 to moles of CO2 with the factor 16 mol CO2 / 25 mol O2. How many significant figures should the answer have?
key: 4, set by 0.3150; the mole ratio is exact
wrong: 2, set by the 16 and the 25 in the ratio
5, because the ratio has 5 digits in total
explanation: Mole ratios are exact, so 4 significant figures, like 0.3150: 0.3150 × 16/25 = 0.2016 mol CO2.

q: Yeast ferment grape sugar into wine: C6H12O6(aq) → 2 C2H5OH(aq) + 2 CO2(g). What mass of ethanol can form from 75.0 g of glucose? (C6H12O6 180.156 g/mol; C2H5OH 46.069 g/mol)
explanation: 75.0 g × (1 mol / 180.156 g) × (2 mol C2H5OH / 1 mol C6H12O6) × (46.069 g / 1 mol) = 38.4 g C2H5OH.

q: An antacid tablet contains 0.750 g of calcium carbonate, which neutralizes stomach acid: CaCO3(s) + 2 HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g). What mass of HCl can it neutralize? (CaCO3 100.09 g/mol; HCl 36.46 g/mol)
explanation: 0.750 g CaCO3 × (1 mol / 100.09 g) × (2 mol HCl / 1 mol CaCO3) × (36.46 g / 1 mol) = 0.546 g HCl. (Context only; follow the label.)

q: Valley farms rely on ammonia fertilizer made by N2(g) + 3 H2(g) → 2 NH3(g). What mass of H2 is needed to make 85.0 g of NH3? (NH3 17.031 g/mol; H2 2.016 g/mol)
explanation: 85.0 g NH3 × (1 mol / 17.031 g) × (3 mol H2 / 2 mol NH3) × (2.016 g / 1 mol) = 15.1 g H2.

q: What mass of O2 must you breathe in to fully oxidize 16.5 g of glucose? C6H12O6 + 6 O2 → 6 CO2 + 6 H2O (C6H12O6 180.156 g/mol; O2 31.998 g/mol)
explanation: 16.5 g × (1 mol / 180.156 g) × (6 mol O2 / 1 mol C6H12O6) × (31.998 g / 1 mol) = 17.6 g O2.

q: Magnesium ribbon burns with a bright white flame: 2 Mg(s) + O2(g) → 2 MgO(s). What mass of MgO forms from 3.65 g of Mg? (Mg 24.31 g/mol; MgO 40.31 g/mol)
explanation: 3.65 g Mg × (1 mol / 24.31 g) × (2 mol MgO / 2 mol Mg) × (40.31 g / 1 mol) = 6.05 g MgO.

q: Many rural Valley homes heat with propane: C3H8(g) + 5 O2(g) → 3 CO2(g) + 4 H2O(l). What mass of CO2 forms when 26.5 g of propane burns? (C3H8 44.097 g/mol; CO2 44.009 g/mol)
explanation: 26.5 g C3H8 × (1 mol / 44.097 g) × (3 mol CO2 / 1 mol C3H8) × (44.009 g / 1 mol) = 79.3 g CO2.

q: Iron rusts by 4 Fe(s) + 3 O2(g) → 2 Fe2O3(s). What mass of O2 is used when 8.40 g of iron rusts completely? (Fe 55.85 g/mol; O2 31.998 g/mol)
explanation: 8.40 g Fe × (1 mol / 55.85 g) × (3 mol O2 / 4 mol Fe) × (31.998 g / 1 mol) = 3.61 g O2.

q: Which order of steps converts grams of a reactant A into grams of a product B?
key: g A → mol A → mol B → g B
wrong: g A → g B, using the coefficients
g A → mol B → mol A → g B
mol A → g A → g B → mol B
explanation: The road map: g A → mol A → mol B → g B (molar mass of A, mole ratio, molar mass of B).

q: A student finds the mass of water made from 5.5 g of H2 with 2 H2(g) + O2(g) → 2 H2O(l) as 5.5 g H2 × (2 mol H2O / 2 mol H2) = 5.5 g H2O. What went wrong?
key: The grams of H2 were never converted to moles, so the mole ratio was used on grams.
wrong: The mole ratio is upside down.
Nothing; the ratio is 1 : 1, so the masses are equal.
explanation: The student skipped the conversion to moles. 5.5 g × (1 mol / 2.016 g) × (2 mol H2O / 2 mol H2) × (18.015 g / 1 mol) = 49 g H2O.

q: Aspirin is made by C7H6O3 + C4H6O3 → C9H8O4 + C2H4O2 (salicylic acid + acetic anhydride → aspirin + acetic acid). What mass of acetic anhydride reacts exactly with 3.45 g of salicylic acid? (C7H6O3 138.122 g/mol; C4H6O3 102.089 g/mol)
explanation: 3.45 g C7H6O3 × (1 mol / 138.122 g) × (1 mol C4H6O3 / 1 mol C7H6O3) × (102.089 g / 1 mol) = 2.55 g C4H6O3.

q: Baking soda releases CO2 when heated in an oven: 2 NaHCO3(s) → Na2CO3(s) + H2O(g) + CO2(g). What mass of CO2 forms from 3.36 g of NaHCO3? (NaHCO3 84.01 g/mol; CO2 44.009 g/mol)
explanation: 3.36 g NaHCO3 × (1 mol / 84.01 g) × (1 mol CO2 / 2 mol NaHCO3) × (44.009 g / 1 mol) = 0.880 g CO2.

q: Bread dough rises as yeast ferment sugar: C6H12O6 → 2 C2H5OH + 2 CO2. The table follows the road map for 30.0 g of glucose. What mass of CO2 goes in the last row?
explanation: 0.3330 mol CO2 × 44.009 g/mol = 14.7 g CO2. Each row is one step of the road map.

q: The thermite reaction welds railroad rails: Fe2O3(s) + 2 Al(s) → Al2O3(s) + 2 Fe(l). What mass of Al reacts exactly with 12.5 g of Fe2O3? (Fe2O3 159.70 g/mol; Al 26.98 g/mol)
explanation: 12.5 g Fe2O3 × (1 mol / 159.70 g) × (2 mol Al / 1 mol Fe2O3) × (26.98 g / 1 mol) = 4.22 g Al.

q: How many moles of HCl are in 35.0 mL of 0.150 M HCl?
explanation: 35.0 mL × (1 L / 1000 mL) × (0.150 mol / 1 L) = 0.00525 mol HCl.

q: Baking soda can neutralize acid: NaHCO3(s) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g). What volume of 0.125 M HCl reacts with 0.315 g of NaHCO3? (NaHCO3 84.01 g/mol)
explanation: 0.315 g × (1 mol / 84.01 g) × (1 mol HCl / 1 mol NaHCO3) × (1 L / 0.125 mol) = 0.0300 L = 30.0 mL.

q: A 3% hydrogen peroxide solution decomposes: 2 H2O2(aq) → 2 H2O(l) + O2(g). What volume of O2 at STP forms from 0.346 mol of H2O2?
explanation: 0.346 mol H2O2 × (1 mol O2 / 2 mol H2O2) × (22.4 L / 1 mol) = 3.88 L O2.

q: Heating limestone in a kiln makes lime for cement and for treating farm soil: CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g). What volume of CO2 at STP forms from 15.0 g of CaCO3? (CaCO3 100.09 g/mol)
explanation: 15.0 g × (1 mol / 100.09 g) × (1 mol CO2 / 1 mol CaCO3) × (22.4 L / 1 mol) = 3.36 L CO2 at STP.

q: In a gas-production lab, magnesium ribbon reacts with acid: Mg(s) + 2 HCl(aq) → MgCl2(aq) + H2(g). What volume of H2, in mL at STP, forms from 0.0425 g of Mg? (Mg 24.31 g/mol)
explanation: 0.0425 g Mg × (1 mol / 24.31 g) × (1 mol H2 / 1 mol Mg) × (22.4 L / 1 mol) = 0.03916 L = 39.2 mL H2.

q: A winemaker ferments grapes at 25 °C and 1 atm, where 1 mol of gas occupies 24.5 L: C6H12O6(aq) → 2 C2H5OH(aq) + 2 CO2(g). What volume of CO2 forms from 12.6 g of glucose? (C6H12O6 180.156 g/mol)
explanation: 12.6 g × (1 mol / 180.156 g) × (2 mol CO2 / 1 mol glucose) × (24.5 L / 1 mol) = 3.43 L CO2.

q: In a titration, H2SO4(aq) + 2 NaOH(aq) → Na2SO4(aq) + 2 H2O(l). What volume of 0.250 M NaOH neutralizes 15.0 mL of 0.180 M H2SO4?
explanation: 0.0150 L × (0.180 mol / 1 L) × (2 mol NaOH / 1 mol H2SO4) × (1 L / 0.250 mol) = 0.0216 L = 21.6 mL NaOH.

q: For which gas sample can you use 22.4 L/mol to convert volume to moles?
wrong: Exhaled air at body temperature, 37 °C, and 1 atm
Helium in a balloon at 25 °C and 1 atm
Oxygen in a compressed tank at 0 °C and 150 atm
explanation: 22.4 L/mol holds only at STP, 0 °C and 1 atm. Chapter 10 handles other conditions.

q: A student finds the moles of NaOH in 25.0 mL of 0.150 M NaOH as 25.0 × 0.150 = 3.75 mol. What went wrong?
key: The volume was not converted to liters; the answer should be 0.00375 mol.
wrong: Molarity is mol per mL, so the answer is right.
The student needed the molar mass of NaOH.
explanation: mL was not converted to L: 25.0 mL = 0.0250 L, and 0.0250 L × 0.150 mol/L = 0.00375 mol NaOH.

q: Zinc dissolves in hydrochloric acid: Zn(s) + 2 HCl(aq) → ZnCl2(aq) + H2(g). What mass of Zn reacts with 40.0 mL of 0.600 M HCl? (Zn 65.39 g/mol)
explanation: 0.0400 L × (0.600 mol / 1 L) × (1 mol Zn / 2 mol HCl) × (65.39 g / 1 mol) = 0.785 g Zn.

q: What is the limiting reactant in a reaction?
key: The reactant that is used up first, which sets the most product that can form
wrong: The reactant present in the smallest mass
The reactant with the smallest coefficient in the balanced equation
The reactant that is left over when the reaction stops
explanation: The limiting reactant is used up first and sets the maximum amount of product; the other reactant is in excess and some is left over.

q: For N2(g) + 3 H2(g) → 2 NH3(g), 1.80 mol of N2 and 4.80 mol of H2 react. What is the maximum amount of NH3 that can form?
explanation: N2 → 3.60 mol NH3; H2 → 3.20 mol NH3. H2 is limiting: 3.20 mol NH3.

q: 6.20 g of Na and 7.10 g of Cl2 react: 2 Na(s) + Cl2(g) → 2 NaCl(s). Which is the limiting reactant? (Na 22.99 g/mol; Cl2 70.90 g/mol)
key: Cl2, because it can make less NaCl
wrong: Na, because its mass is smaller
Na, because the equation needs 2 Na for every Cl2
explanation: Na → 0.2697 mol NaCl; Cl2 → 0.2003 mol NaCl. Cl2 is limiting, even though its mass is larger.

q: 14.0 g of N2 and 3.60 g of H2 react: N2(g) + 3 H2(g) → 2 NH3(g). What is the maximum mass of NH3 that can form? (N2 28.014 g/mol; H2 2.016 g/mol; NH3 17.031 g/mol)
explanation: N2 makes 0.9995 mol NH3, H2 1.190 mol, so N2 limits: 0.9995 mol × 17.031 g/mol = 17.0 g NH3.

q: A catalytic converter removes CO by 2 CO(g) + O2(g) → 2 CO2(g). A mixture of 3.40 mol CO and 2.10 mol O2 reacts. How much of the excess reactant is left over?
explanation: CO is limiting; it uses 1.70 mol O2. Left over: 2.10 − 1.70 = 0.40 mol O2.

q: 6.50 g of iron and 4.25 g of sulfur are heated: Fe(s) + S(s) → FeS(s). What mass of the excess reactant is left? (Fe 55.85 g/mol; S 32.06 g/mol)
explanation: Fe is limiting. S used: 0.1164 mol × 32.06 g/mol = 3.73 g. Left: 4.25 g − 3.73 g = 0.52 g S.

q: The box shows the molecules before N2(g) + 3 H2(g) → 2 NH3(g) runs. What is the most NH3 that can form, and which reactant is limiting?
explanation: H2: 6 × 2/3 = 4 NH3; N2: 3 × 2 = 6 NH3. H2 limits: 4 NH3, and 1 N2 is left.

q: 6.60 g of propane and 20.0 g of O2 react: C3H8(g) + 5 O2(g) → 3 CO2(g) + 4 H2O(l). What is the maximum mass of CO2? (C3H8 44.097 g/mol; O2 31.998 g/mol; CO2 44.009 g/mol)
explanation: O2 → 0.3750 mol CO2 (less than 0.4490 from propane), so O2 limits: 0.3750 × 44.009 = 16.5 g CO2.

q: For 2 H2(g) + O2(g) → 2 H2O(g), a student has 3.4 mol of H2 and 2.0 mol of O2 and says, “O2 is limiting because there are fewer moles of it.” What is wrong with this reasoning?
key: Moles can be compared directly only when the coefficients are equal; here H2 is limiting.
wrong: Nothing; the reactant with fewer moles is always limiting.
The student should compare grams instead of moles.
O2 is limiting, but only because it has the larger molar mass.
explanation: H2 → 3.4 mol H2O; O2 → 4.0 mol H2O. H2 is limiting; compare moles only through the mole ratio.

q: Ammonium sulfate fertilizer forms by 2 NH3(aq) + H2SO4(aq) → (NH4)2SO4(aq). 3.40 g of NH3 and 12.5 g of H2SO4 react. What mass of (NH4)2SO4 can form? (NH3 17.031 g/mol; H2SO4 98.07 g/mol; (NH4)2SO4 132.13 g/mol)
explanation: NH3 → 0.09982 mol; H2SO4 → 0.1275 mol. NH3 limits: 0.09982 × 132.13 = 13.2 g (NH4)2SO4.

q: 5.75 g of Na and 8.15 g of Cl2 react: 2 Na(s) + Cl2(g) → 2 NaCl(s). What mass of the excess reactant remains? (Na 22.99 g/mol; Cl2 70.90 g/mol)
explanation: Cl2 is limiting; it uses 5.29 g Na. Left: 5.75 − 5.29 = 0.46 g Na.

q: For 2 SO2(g) + O2(g) → 2 SO3(g), which mixture in the table reacts with nothing left over?
explanation: Only Mixture B (3.0 mol SO2 : 1.5 mol O2) is in the exact 2 : 1 ratio.

q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 18.6 g, and a student collects 15.9 g of product. What is the percent yield?
What is the theoretical yield of a reaction?
key: The most product that stoichiometry predicts from the limiting reactant
wrong: The mass of product you weigh at the end of the lab
The total mass of all the reactants
The product predicted from the excess reactant
explanation: Theoretical yield = the maximum product calculated from the limiting reactant.

q: Burning 1.20 g of Mg, 2 Mg(s) + O2(g) → 2 MgO(s), gives 1.79 g of MgO. What is the percent yield? (Mg 24.31 g/mol; MgO 40.31 g/mol)
explanation: Theoretical = 1.990 g MgO; 1.79 g ÷ 1.990 g × 100% = 90.0%.

q: In a lab, aspirin is made from salicylic acid and excess acetic anhydride: C7H6O3 + C4H6O3 → C9H8O4 + C2H4O2. What is the theoretical yield of aspirin from 1.38 g of salicylic acid? (C7H6O3 138.122 g/mol; C9H8O4 180.159 g/mol)
explanation: 1.38 g × (1 mol / 138.122 g) × (1 mol C9H8O4 / 1 mol C7H6O3) × (180.159 g / 1 mol) = 1.80 g C9H8O4.

q: A student mixes 2.76 g of salicylic acid with 3.06 g of acetic anhydride, C7H6O3 + C4H6O3 → C9H8O4 + C2H4O2, and collects 2.95 g of aspirin. What is the percent yield? (C7H6O3 138.122 g/mol; C4H6O3 102.089 g/mol; C9H8O4 180.159 g/mol)
explanation: Salicylic acid limits; theoretical = 3.600 g aspirin. 2.95 ÷ 3.600 × 100% = 81.9%.

q: A student filters alum crystals and weighs them right away, reporting a 106% yield. What is the most likely reason?
key: The crystals are still wet, so their mass includes water.
wrong: The reaction made more product than the limiting reactant allows.
Some crystals were lost in the filtrate.
The student used the limiting reactant to find the theoretical yield.
explanation: A yield above 100% points to extra mass: here, water left in the crystals.

q: Which question does a percent yield answer?
key: How much of the possible product did I collect?
wrong: How close is my measurement to the accepted value?
How much of the excess reactant is left?
How fast did the reaction go?
explanation: Percent yield asks how much of the possible product you collected; percent error asks how close a measurement is to the accepted value.

q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 42.5 g. If the percent yield is 76.0%, what mass of product is collected?
explanation: Actual = 0.760 × 42.5 g = 32.3 g.

q: Ethanol for fuel is made by fermenting corn sugar: C6H12O6 → 2 C2H5OH + 2 CO2. From 64.0 g of glucose at an 82.0% yield, what mass of ethanol is collected? (C6H12O6 180.156 g/mol; C2H5OH 46.069 g/mol)
explanation: Theoretical 32.73 g × 0.820 = 26.8 g C2H5OH.

q: In the alum synthesis lab, each Al atom ends up in one formula unit of alum, KAl(SO4)2·12H2O. A student starts with 0.825 g of Al and collects 12.9 g of dry alum. What is the percent yield? (Al 26.98 g/mol; KAl(SO4)2·12H2O 474.37 g/mol; KAl(SO4)2 258.19 g/mol)
explanation: Theoretical = 0.03058 mol × 474.37 g/mol = 14.51 g; 12.9 ÷ 14.51 × 100% = 88.9%.

q: Hydrogen fuel cells run on 2 H2(g) + O2(g) → 2 H2O(l), ΔH = −571.6 kJ. Which describes this reaction?
key: Exothermic: heat is released and the surroundings warm up
wrong: Endothermic: heat is absorbed and the surroundings cool down
Exothermic: heat is absorbed from the surroundings
Endothermic, because ΔH is a large number
explanation: ΔH < 0, so the reaction is exothermic: 571.6 kJ is released per 2 mol H2.

q: An instant cold pack gets cold when ammonium nitrate dissolves in water. Which statement is true about this process?
key: It is endothermic, ΔH > 0: it absorbs heat from your skin.
wrong: It is exothermic, ΔH < 0: it absorbs heat.
It is exothermic, ΔH < 0: cold is released into the pack.
explanation: The cold pack absorbs heat: endothermic, ΔH > 0.

q: Heating limestone is endothermic: CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g), ΔH = +178 kJ. What is ΔH for the reverse reaction, CaO(s) + CO2(g) → CaCO3(s)?
explanation: Reverse reaction: ΔH = −178 kJ (exothermic).

q: Given 2 H2(g) + O2(g) → 2 H2O(l), ΔH = −571.6 kJ, what is ΔH for 4 H2(g) + 2 O2(g) → 4 H2O(l)?
explanation: 2 × (−571.6 kJ) = −1143.2 kJ.

q: For 2 H2(g) + O2(g) → 2 H2O(l), ΔH = −571.6 kJ, how much heat is released when 1.35 mol of O2 reacts?
explanation: 1.35 mol O2 × (571.6 kJ / 1 mol O2) = 772 kJ released.

q: A propane camp stove burns fuel by C3H8(g) + 5 O2(g) → 3 CO2(g) + 4 H2O(l), ΔH = −2.220 × 103 kJ. How much heat is released when 5.00 g of propane burns? (C3H8 44.097 g/mol)
explanation: 5.00 g × (1 mol / 44.097 g) × (2.220 × 103 kJ / 1 mol C3H8) = 252 kJ released.

q: A Valley dairy digester burns captured methane, CH4(g) + 2 O2(g) → CO2(g) + 2 H2O(l), ΔH = −890.3 kJ. What mass of methane must burn to release 3.60 × 104 kJ? (CH4 16.043 g/mol)
explanation: 3.60 × 104 kJ × (1 mol CH4 / 890.3 kJ) × (16.043 g / 1 mol) = 649 g CH4.

q: Your cells oxidize glucose: C6H12O6 + 6 O2 → 6 CO2 + 6 H2O, ΔH = −2803 kJ. How much heat is released by 5.40 g of glucose? (C6H12O6 180.156 g/mol)
explanation: 5.40 g × (1 mol / 180.156 g) × (2803 kJ / 1 mol) = 84.0 kJ released.

q: A food label counts the energy in carbohydrates in Calories (1 Cal = 4.184 kJ). Using C6H12O6 + 6 O2 → 6 CO2 + 6 H2O, ΔH = −2803 kJ, how many Calories does 12.0 g of glucose release? (C6H12O6 180.156 g/mol)
explanation: 12.0 g × (1 mol / 180.156 g) × (2803 kJ / 1 mol) × (1 Cal / 4.184 kJ) = 44.6 Cal, about 3.7 Cal per gram.

q: Decomposing limestone absorbs heat: CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g), ΔH = +178 kJ. How much heat is needed to decompose 35.0 g of CaCO3? (CaCO3 100.09 g/mol)
explanation: 35.0 g × (1 mol / 100.09 g) × (178 kJ / 1 mol) = 62.2 kJ absorbed.
